long.say: Meet Mac Cleanup. A free, local tool that keeps a developer's Mac light, and safe.
If you build software on a Mac, junk piles up quietly. Xcode DerivedData, old simulators, stale node modules, and caches from every package manager.
Mac Cleanup puts it all in one place. Everything runs on your machine. Nothing is uploaded, and nothing is deleted without your say.
Press Scan. It checks caches, simulators, old IDE versions, and your project folders.
Results come back as cards. Green items are safe caches that rebuild themselves, so they're pre-selected. Amber items need your judgement.
Open any card to see exactly which folders it found, and how big each one is.
Want an amber item gone too? Just tap it. The dock at the bottom keeps a running total.
When you're happy, hit Clean selected, and confirm.
Twenty five gigabytes back, in seconds. The free space ring updates right away.
Next, security. One click audits your firewall, disk encryption, sharing services, startup items, and even private keys left lying in Downloads.
The network check lists every service open to your network, with the program behind it, and flags risky ones like an exposed Redis, or Screen Sharing.
The Applications check looks at every installed app. It catches broken code signatures, end of life software, remote access tools, and anything Homebrew says is out of date.
Live traffic measures who is sending data right now. Here, an unsigned program hidden in a cache folder is uploading four megabytes a second. Exactly what you want to catch.
Want ongoing protection? Turn on the background watcher. It alerts you when something new opens a port, or your router or DNS changes. It's off by default.
It follows your system theme, and looks just as good in light mode.
Prefer the terminal? Everything is also a command, with dry runs by default.
Install it as a native Mac app, double click the one click setup, or use the command line. It's a single Python file with no dependencies, and one hundred and fifteen automated tests.
No root access. No telemetry. Deletes happen only inside your home folder, and only after you confirm.
Mac Cleanup. A lighter machine, and a safer one.
